home_hero_subheading: Premium apparel for the stories we dream of & the ones that ruin us — designed with the quiet grandeur of an antique library and made to be lived in.
home_story_heading: Built for the Nights You Read Past Midnight
home_story_paragraph1: Vow & Vice began with a simple ache — the way a certain kind of story lodges itself under your ribs and stays there. The candlelit libraries. The vows made in ruin. The quiet, dangerous kind of devotion that only exists in the best romances and the oldest myths.
home_story_paragraph2: We didn't want merchandise. We wanted clothing that felt like that ache — heirloom detailing, antique gold, deep botanical color, fabric that feels like it already has a history. Every piece is designed the way a favorite passage is written: with intention, restraint, and just enough danger.
about_intro: There is a particular kind of person who finishes a story and doesn't want to leave it. Who closes the cover, or the tab, or the final page, and still feels the candlelight on their skin — the old libraries, the vows made too fast, the villains who were really just the misunderstood. Vow & Vice was built for that person. It was built for us.
about_section1_text: We didn't want to make clothing that referenced a title on a shelf. We wanted to make clothing that felt like the feeling itself — the ache of romantasy, the hush of dark academia, the glint of a sword half-hidden in roses. Every piece we design starts with a mood board of antique engravings, celestial maps, and heirloom jewelry long before it ever touches a sketch of a garment. The story comes first. The clothing follows.
about_section2_text: Nothing at Vow & Vice is mass-produced. Each piece is made to order, in small batches, so that what you receive feels considered rather than churned out. It takes longer. We think it's worth it — the same way a favorite book is worth rereading slowly, underlining the parts that matter.
about_section3_text: You don't need to have read a particular series to wear Vow & Vice. You just need to know the feeling — the pull toward something romantic and a little dangerous, something old and gilded and slightly unwell. If that's you, welcome. We saved you a seat by the fire.
